title: Staged release telemetry contracts and automated mitigation matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: After a recent staged deployment that degraded tail latency and increased token-level error rates for a subset of customers, we need a formalized set of telemetry contracts and an automated mitigation matrix that governs transitions from shadow -> canary -> production. This ticket coordinates runbook updates, console/alerting configuration, and the implementation of auto-mitigation heuristics (including safe auto-rollback) tied to multi-signal detection.

Goals:
- Define a minimal telemetry contract that every staged-release must emit (latency P50/P95/P99, error-rate by route/model, top-5 user-agent buckets, token-level decode error spikes, KV-cache hit rate, prefix cache miss ratio, model variant mismatch rate).
- Create a mitigation matrix that maps detected violations (single-signal or multi-signal) to deterministic actions: traffic shift percentages, temporary rate-limits, canary freeze, automated rollback, and escalation.
- Implement statistical heuristics for auto-rollback: rolling window, minimum sample size, and multi-signal confirmation to minimize false positives.
- Update staged deployment runbook with step-by-step checks and safety gate preconditions (observability, test prompts, canary cohort size, ramp schedule).
- Add console indicators and an opt-in automation toggle per project (required for enterprise Dedicated/Private tenants).

Scope notes and constraints:
- Automation must be opt-in and have a manual override. For customer-impacting models (customer_impact=high) the system should prefer controlled traffic shifts and alerts over blind rollbacks.
- We prioritize multi-signal rules (e.g., P95 latency regression + token-level decode error increase + KV cache miss spike) to trigger automated rollback. Single noisy signals can create churn.
- This work interfaces with existing rollout infra; will require changes in routing policy layer and the rollout controller.

Deliverables:
1) telemetry-contracts.md (confluence) authored and reviewed;
2) mitigation-matrix.csv for engineering/ops;
3) automation prototype (controller + e2e tests) behind feature flag;
4) runbook updates and playbook snippets for on-call;
5) console UI for safety toggle and incident reason trace.

Success criteria:
- All staged releases emit required metrics and are validated in pre-canary check (90%+ in 48h).
- Automated mitigation correctly reduces user-impacting errors in at least 2/3 simulated degradation scenarios in staging.
- Runbook audit completed and adopted by SRE and Product teams.
comments: 2025-03-10: Ticket created during postmortem sync after the March 9th canary regression. Owner: Aisha. Initial scope approved by Eng Leads.
2025-03-12: Spike results: discovered insufficient visibility into per-route token decode errors; added instrument point in runtime (PR #1487). Branch: feat/telemetry-decode-errors.

2025-03-14: RFC posted: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/TELEMETRY-RFC. Reviewed by Sophia Lin (PM) and Jordan Cole (SRE). Major decision: require multi-signal confirmation and 95% statistical confidence for auto-rollback; keep default auto-rollback disabled for customer_impact=high.

2025-03-16: Prototype automation deployed to staging with shadow traffic. First runs show correct decision logging; observed one false-positive on a noisy upstream metric — increased smoothing window to 10 minutes.
2025-03-18: Design review complete. Marcelo to open PR for controller changes and add e2e test. Runbook draft uploaded and assigned to on-call rotation leads for feedback before canary next week.
Next steps: finalize mitigation matrix, land controller PR, create canary dashboard template, schedule dry-run with SRE on 2025-03-24.
